title: Corn Meal-Brod (Corn Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with cornmeal, yeast, and wheat flour.

ingredients.name: 2 large tablespoons homemade or 1 cent baker's yeast
ingredients.sourceText: 2 large tablespoons homemade or 1 cent baker's yeast

steps: Blend 2 quarts cornmeal with 3 pints hot water.
Add {{source-2}}, {{source-3}}, and 2 large tablespoons homemade or 1 cent baker's yeast.
Let stand 5 hours in a warm place.
Add {{source-5}} and 3/4 pint hot water.
Let it rise again for 1 1/2 hours, knead lightly, and divide into bread pans, letting them stand a few minutes before putting them in.
Bake in a moderate oven for 1 1/2 hours.

title: Corned Beef Fogt (Boiled Salted Beef)
description: Prepared with beef and water.
steps: The meat is placed in water overnight if it is very salty, but if the meat is young and only lightly salted, such prolonged soaking is not necessary.
The salt is washed off, and cold water is poured over to completely cover it.
It should be placed over so slow a fire that it will only simmer, and remain thus for 4 to 6 hours according to the size of the piece.
If it is tough, let it stand over until the next day and bring it to the boiling point just before serving.
Breast pieces are simmered until the bones are easily removed, folded together and placed under a weight until cold; then it can be sliced.

title: Cranberry Pie (Trane Bær Pie)
description: A pastry dish made with cranberries, corn starch, and dough.
steps: Pick the cranberries clean, wash in cold water, and set over heat with cold water that covers them.
Let them boil gently until they are soft.
Press them through a sieve with a spoon.
Set them over heat again with sufficient sugar and {{source-3}} dissolved in a little of the juice that has been held back and must be cold.
When it comes to a boil it is done.
Line the form with dough prepared meanwhile.
Pour the berries over and lay strips of dough on top in various figures.
Bake in a moderately heated oven.
To take away the bitter taste of the cranberries, one may boil a peeled and cut apple among them.

title: Cream Pie No. 1
description: A pastry dish made with corn starch, lemon juice, and white sugar.
steps: Boil 1 scant pint fresh milk.
In a little of the cold milk, stir 2 small tablespoons corn starch and beat together with 2 eggs.
When the milk has boiled, slowly stir this in with 1 scant teacup sugar, {{source-4}}, and {{source-5}}.
For the cake, stir together 3 eggs with {{source-7}}, {{source-8}}, {{source-9}} sifted together with {{source-10}}.
Pour into two ordinary pie plates and bake in a hot oven.
When the cake is done, take it out, split while still warm, and fill the cream between both layers.
If desired, it can be glazed again with egg white and sugar.

title: Creme Sauce (Cream Sauce)
description: A sauce made with cream, egg yolks, and whipped cream.
steps: Boil 1 Quart good sweet Cream with {{source-1}} and a little Vanilla.
Thicken it with 8 well-beaten Egg yolks, and whip it well.
When it is cold, add whipped Cream, about 5 to 6 Tablespoons, which is gently stirred in and should be seen on top.
This Sauce is used cold for Red Wine Pudding, Lemon Pudding, Fromage and several similar Things.
It is also used for Blanc-Manger; but then it is mixed with twice as much whipped Cream.

title: Creme-Ablekage (Cream Apple Cake)
description: A cake made with cream, apples, and jam or raspberry or cherry.
steps: Peel apples and cut off a lid, hollowing them out
Simmer in sugar and a little water so they do not fall apart
Arrange them close together in a fairly deep pan and fill with jam without liquid, preferably raspberry or cherry marmalade
Cover with the cut-off lids
Make a cream from 1 quart cream, 8 egg yolks, a little vanilla, half a tablespoon corn starch, and sugar to taste
When cold, pour the cream over the apples
Place the pan in the oven and bake the cake slowly
When the batter begins to set and becomes light brown, it is done

ingredients.name: 4 pieces of isinglass dissolved in insignificant water

ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 L (1 Pægl) cream for whipped cream

steps: Whisk together four egg yolks white with {{source-1}}
Bring {{source-2}} to a boil and stir it into the egg mixture, which is again poured into the pot and stirred well until it comes to a boil
Pour it out and add a few drops of vanilla essence
Stir in 4 pieces of isinglass dissolved in insignificant water together with 2 glasses of sherry and as much white wine or rhubarb juice so that the sauce gets a fresh, tart flavor
Stir regularly in the cream until it is cold
When it is to be served, stir in whipped cream made from 1/2 L (1 Pægl) cream, and if the sauce is desired thinner, it can simply be diluted with a little cream
The sauce can be colored pale pink with fruit coloring and served with various cold puddings
It can be varied with: strawberry juice, raspberry juice, cherry marmalade, ginger, orange essence, or maraschino or cacao liqueur

steps: Line the bottom of a pot with slices of bacon.
Place the turkey on top and steam until tender for approximately 3 hours in a little broth or water to which salt, a few halved carrots, and a celery stalk have been added.

title: Dronning-Suppe à la reine (Queen's Soup)
description: A soup made with hen, beef, and veal.
steps: Afvadskes En fed Høne, 4 Pd. Oxekjød og 3 Pd. Kalvekjød i koldt Vand og sættes over Ilden med en Theskefuld Salt og saa meget Vand, at det netop staar over Kjødet.
Naar Suppen er skummet, tilføjes 1 Selleri, nogle Persillerødder, 2 Løg og nogle Korn hvidt Peber.
Naar Hønen er mør, tages den op; men det Øvrige koges endnu i en Time og sies da.
Det Fede skummes af Suppen, kommes i en anden Kasserolle med 2 til 3 Spiseskefulde Hvedemel og bages godt sammen, dog ikke saaledes, at det brunes.
Det spædes med den afkogte Hønsebouillon og faar et Opkog.
Brystet af Hønen skæres i fine Strimler paa et Par Tommers Længde, og ved Anretningen kommes nogle Stykker i hver Tallerken.
Piskes 6 Æggeblommer i Terrinen med 6 Spiseskefulde god sød Fløde, og den kogende Suppe hældes herpaa under stadig Piskning.
Til Suppen kan serveres afbagt Brød.

title: Dyreryg (Saddle of Venison)
description: Prepared with venison, meat, and carrots.

ingredients.name: One saddle of venison, approximately 10 pounds
ingredients.sourceText: One saddle of venison, approximately 10 pounds

ingredients.name: Strips of salted meat, very thin and approximately 2 inches long
ingredients.sourceText: Strips of salted meat, very thin and approximately 2 inches long

steps: Take one approximately 10 pounds in weight and lard it with strips of salted meat, very thin and approximately 2 inches long, two rows on each side.
Slice two carrots and one onion and season with a little salted meat, sliced thin, in a large roasting pan.
Add two bay leaves, two cloves, five grains of allspice, half a lemon sliced thin, a little salt and pepper.
Place the venison saddle in the pan with one quarter soup stock (Claret) and a small lump of butter, and let it simmer approximately one quarter of an hour on top of the stove.
Set it then in a hot oven to roast, and drip with a little butter every fifth minute, until it is half-roasted, so the blood runs out when you cut into the meat.
Serve with wine sauce. Others prefer it completely tender. Then it must be roasted much longer. Serve with cream sauce.

title: Engelsk Boeuf (English Beef)
description: Prepared with beef or tenderloin, onion, and gravy or stock.

ingredients.name: Beef tenderloin or neck piece, not freshly slaughtered but aged several days
ingredients.sourceText: Beef tenderloin or neck piece, not freshly slaughtered but aged several days

steps: Cut the meat into appropriately sized pieces and place them on a dry, strongly heated pan.
Fry the pieces at brisk heat so they remain juicy inside, and as they are done, place them on the serving dish and pour over them the juice that has run from the meat.
When all pieces are fried, add butter to the pan and stir well with a spoon to loosen the gravy that still clings to it.
Add finely chopped red onion to this, cook it a little with it, then add more gravy and pepper.
Alternatively, when the meat is cut into appropriately thick slices, beat these, dip them in chopped red onion and a little pepper, and place them on a pan in which you have browned some butter.
Fry the slices over a brisk heat, turn them as soon as they begin to brown, and under no circumstances fry them so much that the meat becomes dry.
Stir up the sauce on the pan with gravy and pour it over the pieces.
Serve with boiled, peeled potatoes; sometimes with a fried egg on top.
Calculate 3 portions from one pound of meat.

title: Engelsk Frugt-Pie (English Fruit Pie)
description: A pastry dish made with butter or margarine, apple or apples, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: cooked apple pieces or raw peeled apples
ingredients.sourceText: cooked apple pieces or raw peeled apples

steps: Make a pastry dough as for butter dough, using the specified amounts of butter, flour, water and baking powder
Roll out the dough 3 times, handling it as little as possible with the hands but working it with a broad knife
Roll out a very thin sheet of dough and line a buttered form with it
Lay cooked apple pieces or raw peeled apples in layers with powdered sugar in the lined form until almost full
Lay another sheet over and press the edges together; this can be crimped with the fingers
Roll out the remaining dough and cut into strips or shapes; arrange these over the pie, brushed with egg white; brush the decoration with egg as well
Bake for 1 hour at even top and bottom heat
All kinds of fruit can be used

title: Engelsk Harvey-Sauce til Kød- og Fiskeretter (English Harvey Sauce for Meat and Fish Dishes)
description: A sauce made with soy sauce, celery seed, and mustard.
steps: Place {{source-1}}, 75 gr (15 kvint) crushed celery seed, 75 gr (15 kvint) mustard seed, 15 gr (3 kvint) ground ginger, a little nutmeg and cayenne pepper, 20 gr (4 kvint) garlic, 75 gr (15 kvint) pickled, chopped cucumbers and {{source-9}} in {{source-0}}.
Cook all this together until it has reduced to approximately half.
Remove from heat and add dried peel of one lemon.
Let the sauce stand covered for a few days and strain before pouring into dry bottles, which are stoppered well.
This sauce, as well as No. 740, can be used instead of the expensive English sauces available in commerce.
Use in sauce for meat and fish dishes and is used much for cold buffets.

title: Faresteg og Sammesteg (Roasted Mutton and Lamb)
description: Prepared with mutton or lamb, bread dough, and butter.

ingredients.name: Bread dough (made from French bread, milk, butter, eggs, sugar, salt)
ingredients.sourceText: Bread dough (made from French bread, milk, butter, eggs, sugar, salt)

steps: There is a skin on the sides of the mutton roast which must be removed before roasting.

The roast is washed, after which many lard it with parsley, which is done by making holes with a knife, one beside the other down the back of the leg of the roast, and pressing picked and washed parsley together with a little butter into each hole.

The roast can be filled with parsley and butter or with bread dough, which is made as follows: some slices of French bread are dipped in milk, left standing for about an hour, and then pounded into pieces with a spoon. A piece of cold butter is stirred until creamy, into which the bread is stirred, along with 1 or 2 eggs, a little sugar and salt.
When well mixed, it is filled into the roast, after this is opened from one side, so that a hand can be gotten in and with this the skin can be loosened as much as possible on the roast.
If there are holes in the roast they are sewn together, and when the dough is in the roast, it is sewn shut.
The roast is dusted with flour and roasted in a good hour.
Lamb is treated in all respects as mutton roast.

title: Fars af Oxekjød (Minced Beef Mixture)
description: Prepared with beef, beef fat, and shallot.

ingredients.name: beef, preferably from the inner part, cut into strips
ingredients.sourceText: 1 pound beef, preferably from the inner part, cut into strips

ingredients.name: a little over 1/4 pound beef fat (30 quints), picked apart and without membrane

ingredients.name: ground spices such as nutmeg, ginger, allspice or cloves to taste
ingredients.sourceText: ground spices such as nutmeg, ginger, allspice or cloves to taste

ingredients.name: 2 eggs or egg whites (optional if cream is used)

steps: Cut the beef into strips and scrape along the sinews to remove them before chopping (or omit if using a meat grinder)
During chopping, blend the beef with the fat
When the beef and fat are well worked together and chopped fine enough to hold together, chop in salt, pepper, shallot, and wheat flour
Allow the mixture to rest for several hours or longer before use
After resting, work it with a spoon and gradually add, at long intervals, a good pail of sweet milk or cream
Blend in ground spices such as nutmeg, ginger, allspice or cloves to taste
Stir the mixture strongly and continuously, making it more cohesive by adding a couple of eggs or egg whites if cream was not used
If desired, the mixture may rest for a few hours and then be stirred with a little more milk to make it firmer
If marrow is available, cut some into small cubes and blend these with the mixture
Test the consistency by forming one ball and cooking it in soup
To form balls: take a larger portion of dough on a large spoon, and using a small spoon dipped in soup between each time, form the balls and place them in the soup

title: Faste-Kringler (Lenten Rings)
description: Prepared with powdered sugar, eggs, and flour.
steps: Whip 6 eggs in a quarter hour with two large tablespoons powdered sugar.
Stir as much of {{source-2}} as it can take into it, and then knead it on a baking board with the rest, but hold back as much as is needed to dust the board with during kneading.
The dough must be worked well and kneaded so long that it completely releases from hands and board, then cut it into small pieces, approximately 18 to 20, which are equal in size.

Roll these with the hands, but without flour on the board, into sausages of a finger's thickness, shape them into rings or wreaths, place them in a pot with plenty of gently and strongly boiling water and boil until they rise, then remove them and bake at once very slowly until quite light.
Do not put so many rings in the water at once that they come to lie on top of one another.
If the rings do not quickly rise, they have settled on the bottom and must then be carefully loosened with a spoon.

title: Ferskener med Cognac (Peaches with Cognac)
description: Prepared with peaches, cognac, and sugar.
steps: Boil the sugar and water into a fairly smooth syrup in which the whole peaches boil for 3 minutes and are then placed in glass jars or crocks, which are left covered for 3 to 4 days.
After this time has elapsed, pour off the syrup, reduce it until it is very smooth, and pour it over the peaches.
The jars must not be filled completely, as after the fruit has cooled, a generous amount of good Cognac must be added before the jars are sealed.

title: Figaro (for 12 Persons)
description: Prepared with sausages, potatoes, and sausage.
steps: Rinse the sausages well and place them in boiling water to cook for 4 to 5 minutes.
Make a roux from butter and flour, then thin it with the water in which the sausages were cooked until it becomes a regular smooth white sauce.
Chop the onions coarsely and cook them tender in the sauce.
On a slightly deep plate, layer slices of boiled potatoes, then slices of the cooked sausages, then another layer of potato slices.
Season the sauce with salt, Maggi Bouillon cubes, and pepper, and pour it over generously, as some will be absorbed by the potatoes.
Sprinkle the dish with bread crumbs and place it in a warm oven to heat through and brown slightly on top.
If no warm oven is available, cut the potatoes and sausages while warm and pour the hot sauce over them.
Serve as soon as it is arranged. Figaro can be served as a lunch or dinner course.

title: Fin Melkesuppe, varm eller kold (Fine Milk Soup, Warm or Cold)
description: A soup made with milk, corn starch or rice flour, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: 1 small dessert spoon corn starch or rice flour
ingredients.sourceText: 1 small dessert spoon corn starch or rice flour

ingredients.name: a couple of drops of vanilla (or a couple of pieces of whole cinnamon)
ingredients.sourceText: a couple of drops of vanilla (or a couple of pieces of whole cinnamon)

steps: Mix the corn starch or rice flour with some of the cold milk
Heat the rest of the milk on the fire, and when it is hot, stir in the flour and cook the milk until it is smooth
Stir the egg yolks with white sugar, thin them with warm milk, and pour into the pot and stir until it begins to cook
Then pour it into a tureen with a little salt and a couple of drops of vanilla added (or cook a couple of pieces of whole cinnamon in the milk instead of vanilla)
Soft poached egg whites may be laid on top in the tureen; the milk in which they cook should contain sugar and a little cinnamon, which milk is then strained and added to the rest of the milk
Serve the soup with small rusks or baked bread, and one generally counts one quart of milk for 3 people

title: Fine engelske Pickles (Fine English Pickles)
description: Prepared with vinegar, mustard seeds, and wine.

ingredients.name: whole Mustard Seeds per glass
ingredients.sourceText: 1 Teaspoon whole Mustard Seeds per glass

steps: Cook all these parts and place in a large crock, let it stand covered until cooled
Add as many cleaned and flaked carrots as needed to color the vinegar yellow

Clean and polish the various vegetables such as cabbage, sliced cauliflower, Brussels sprouts, green beans, small corn, very young elderberry stems, celery, apple slices, cucumbers, small whole peeled mushrooms and the like
Pour boiled vinegar over them repeatedly, cooling each time, until they are soft
Drain on a sieve and let stand overnight
Place in pickle glasses and fill with the aforementioned vinegar
Stopper and bind with bladder
Cover with sealing wax
Add 1-2 bags of Spanish pepper and one teaspoon of whole mustard seeds to each glass

title: Fingerkage (Finger Cakes)
description: A cake made with eggs, sugar, and cream of tartar.
steps: Beat eggs lightly and add {{source-1}}.
Sift in a very scant teaspoon of cream of tartar and half as much soda and a little salt.
Sift in flour until a stiff dough is formed.
Roll the dough fairly thin and spread the remaining sugar over it.
Cut the dough into strips about the size of a finger and place on a buttered pan without touching each other.
Bake in a quick oven and watch that they do not burn.
Vanilla may be stirred into the dough.

title: Fint Hvedebrod paa en anden Maade (Fine Wheat Bread, Another Way)
description: A bread preparation made with yeast, wheat flour, and milk.
steps: Warm 1 small quart milk and pour into the dough pan. Dissolve 1 cent compressed yeast in a little lukewarm water and add to the milk.
Sift in as much flour while stirring to make a thick, even dough that cannot be kneaded, only stirred.
Let it rise for the usual time during the day or overnight.
When risen, add {{source-3}}, {{source-4}}, and {{source-5}}.
Sift in enough flour to make a good, soft dough that can be handled.
Knead well and place in the pan, allowing it to rise again.
When sufficiently risen, divide into as many loaves as desired—2 large or 3 small—let stand for a quarter hour in a warm place, then bake as usual.

title: Fint Rugbrod med Kommen (Fine Rye Bread with Caraway)
description: A bread preparation made with caraway seeds, rye flour, and yeast.
steps: The evening before baking, boil 2 cents caraway seeds in about 3 cups water until the water turns brown.
Pour the hot liquid over fine rye flour and stir quickly to make an even dough.
When cooled, stir in 2 cents baker's yeast.
Cover well and let stand until the next day.
Knead up with wheat flour (and also rye flour if desired) and set to rise again before shaping into loaves.
Bake with good heat.

title: Fish Pie
description: A pastry dish made with fish, potatoes, and salt.
steps: Boil potatoes in well-salted water.
Soak 0.5 small loaf in cold water and wring dry in a clean cloth.
Stir in a little salt, pepper, and {{source-5}}.

When the potatoes are sufficiently cooked, pick them, press through a colander, and season with pepper and salt.
Grease a pudding form on the bottom with butter and lay alternating layers of bread and fish in it.
On top place a neat layer of the potato mixture and bake for one hour in a not too hot oven.

ingredients.sourceText: Salt water fish such as cod or mackerel

Remove and pick out all the bones.
In a casserole, blend {{source-2}} with 1 quart cream or good milk, adding it little by little.

Pour a little sauce into a deep dish, place the fish in it and pour the remaining sauce over.
Beat the whites of 6 eggs to a foam, spread over the top and bake until light brown in the oven.

description: Prepared with fish, butter or marrow, and cream.

ingredients.name: cold butter, or half butter and half marrow

steps: Rinse the fish and cut it open from the back

The fish can be kept until the next day by tying it at the tail so blood and slime can drain away
Wash it again before scraping

title: Fiske-Filet (Fish Fillet)
description: Prepared with bread crumbs, fat, and egg.

ingredients.name: Bread crumbs dried in the oven
ingredients.sourceText: Bread crumbs dried in the oven

steps: Fillet is made only from flatfish.
Wash the flatfish, dry in a clean cloth and place flat on the table.
Cut off the fins with a sharp, thin-bladed knife.

Press the knife down in the middle of the fish until it reaches the bones, then turn it with the edge toward the fins and guide it along the bones outward so that a whole quarter of the fish is loosened from the bones.
In the same way loosen the other quarters and place them all with skin down on the table.
Set one of the fingers of the left hand firmly on the end of one of the quarters and let the knife run along the skin so that the fish piece is freed from it.
Skin all the fillet in this way and place it on a plate.
The whole is a matter of skill, and what it is about is that the fillet does not fall to pieces.
Sprinkle bread crumbs, which have been dried in the oven, crushed fine and sifted, on the table; beat an egg with a spoonful of cold water.
Place the fillet on the crumbs, press lightly, turn, press again, dip in the beaten egg and take away quickly so that the crumbs are not washed off.
Place it again in the crumbs and press in a neat form with the knife.

Heat as much fat as will be sufficient to cover three or four fillets until it begins to smoke; place the fillets in one at a time, fry them light brown, take them up with a skimming ladle and place them for a moment on brown paper so that they are freed from fat.
Place them neatly on a plate with a few parsley leaves and serve them.

ingredients.name: Almost half a pint of sour cream
ingredients.sourceText: Almost half a pint of sour cream

steps: Cut the fish into pieces and boil in 4 quarts of water with salt, a bundle of herbs and root vegetables.

Cook out the fish completely, crush it and strain it; pour a little hot water on it in the strainer to extract the flavor.

title: Fiskebudding (Fish Pudding)
description: A pudding made with fish, melted butter, and wheat flour.

ingredients.name: Fish, preferably Pike, scraped free of skin and bone
ingredients.sourceText: 4 Pounds Fish, preferably Pike, scraped free of skin and bone

steps: Scrape the fish free of skin and bone, then chop it with half a pound of cold butter.
Place the mixture in a mortar and pound it, adding the melted butter gradually during pounding until it becomes like a tough dough and releases from the mortar.
Add 8 eggs one at a time, stirring constantly.
Add 4 tablespoons of wheat flour, salt and pepper to taste, and enough sweet cream so that the mixture becomes appropriately thick.
Test the consistency by placing a spoonful in boiling water; if too thin, add more flour; if too firm, add more cream.
Grease a pudding mold with butter and fill it with the mixture.
Cook for a couple of hours.
Serve with Caper sauce or Crayfish sauce.

Scrape, chop finely and pound with the butter and flour together with salt until it becomes a tough mass
Then stir with quite small amounts of milk at a time
Use only ground white pepper as seasoning
By using potato flour there is considerably more forcemeat, but you can take half wheat flour and half potato flour, though the milk must then be calculated accordingly
It does not tolerate being as soft for balls and meatballs as for pudding and border mold
If the fish is cleaned the day before, bind it, hang by the tail and keep in a cool place
Garfish can be made into forcemeat, but then care must be taken that the dark stripe closest to the skin does not get in

title: Fleſkepandekage (Bacon Pancake)
description: Prepared with bacon, cream, and eggs.
steps: Use, for example, 8 eggs, and to each egg take a spoonful of cream.
Beat the eggs first and then together with the cream.
Brown a little butter in a frying pan, then pour a large spoonful of the batter onto it and lay slices of bacon (which must first be soaked in water) on it.
Pour the batter gently over so the bacon is covered and fry the cake over gentle heat.
Sometimes you must insert a little butter at the edge, as you must not have too much underneath at first.
When it begins to stiffen on top, it is brown underneath and must be turned; it may also happen that it browns while it is still soft on top, in which case the heat is too high.
Slide it from the pan, preferably onto a lid with a handle; place the pan on top of the cake, on which a little butter has first been placed, and hold the lid firmly to the pan as you turn it around.
You can sprinkle chopped parsley on top.

Sprinkle the cake with grated bread and bake for 1 hour.

Turn the cabbage once in a while.
When done, cut the pork and arrange it in the center of the serving dish with the cabbage around it.

title: Forloren Hare (Mock Hare)
description: Prepared with beef, pork, and rusks.
steps: Scrape and mince the meat finely together with the crushed rusks, eggs, salt, and a few spoonfuls of cream.
Form the forcemeat in the shape of a hare saddle.

Roast in the oven for 1 hour, basting frequently with milk.
For the sauce, brown butter and flour, thin with gravy, and before serving add a little raw cream and food coloring.
Garnish with browned potatoes and parsley.
Serve with currant or lingonberry jelly.

description: A sauce made with bouillon or fish or meat stock, egg yolks, and lemon juice.

The sauce must be bound just before serving

title: Forloren Mayonnaise (False Mayonnaise)
description: Prepared with broth, egg yolks, and salad oil.
steps: Make a roux from butter and flour and thin it with enough broth to make a very thick sauce, thickened with the well-beaten egg yolks.
Pour out the sauce and stir until it is cold.
Under constant stirring add salt, pepper, tarragon vinegar, and 4 tablespoons of salad oil, all to taste.
This mayonnaise is easy to make and is preferred by many over the genuine version since it does not contain as much oil.

title: Forloren Skildpaddesuppe (Mock Turtle Soup)
description: A soup made with peppercorns, onions, and wheat flour.

ingredients.name: en halv Pægl Madeira eller Sherry
ingredients.sourceText: en halv Pægl Madeira eller Sherry

steps: Lægges Hovedet af en Fedekalv en Timestid i koldt Vand.
Skylles det med varmt Vand, saa det bliver frit for Blod.
Efter at det er omhyggeligt renset, Ørene afskaarne og Øjnene udtagne, sættes det over Ilden med tilstrækkeligt koldt Vand.
Naar det netop staar paa Kog, tages det op og blancheres ved at overhældes med koldt Vand.
Flækkes Hovedet, og Hjernen udtages.
Suppen sættes paany over Ilden tilligemed Hovedet, lidt Salt, en Suppevisk, 10 hele Peberkorn og et lille Stykke Ingefær.
Den koges derpaa over sagte Ild, indtil Kjødet er godt gjennemkogt og let kan løsnes fra Benene.
Hovedet tages derpaa op, lægges paa et fladt Fad for at afkøles, og Suppen sies.
Et finthakket Rødløg brunes langsomt med et Fjerdingspund Smør og fire Spiseskefulde Hvedemel.
3 Potter kraftig Sky tilsættes, og det Hele spædes med den paa Kalvehovedet kogte Suppe.

Naar det har kogt noget, lægges Kjødet af Kalvehovedet, der er pillet af Benene og tilligemed Tungen skaaret i smaa Stykker, omtrent en halv Tomme paa hver Led, deri tilligemed en lille Knivspidsfuld Kajennepeber og en lille Spiseskefuld Kandis.
Umiddelbart før Anretningen kommes en Spiseskefuld god Cognac og en halv Pægl Madeira eller Sherry i Suppen.
I Terrinen lægges 12 til 20 haardkogte Æggeblommer, hvorefter Suppen ophældes og anrettes.

title: Forlorne Æg (Poached Eggs)
description: Prepared with eggs, water, and salt.
steps: Fresh eggs are cracked on the edge of a plate and placed in a pan with boiling water, which stands over the heat.
You must not put too many in at once, and if you want the yolk clear, there must not be so much water in the pan that it stands over the eggs.
They are loosened with a knife, taken up and wiped off.
For breakfast, they can be served with anchovies, one of which is laid around the yolk on each egg, after the head and backbone have first been removed, or gravy can be laid over them in strips.
If the eggs are not newly laid, add a little vinegar to the water.

title: Fransk Bøf med Maître d'Hôtel-Smør (French Beef with Maître d'Hôtel Butter)
description: Prepared with butter, beef or tenderloin or veal or pork, and gravy or stock.

ingredients.name: beef tenderloin, or veal or pork tenderloin
ingredients.sourceText: 1.5 kg beef tenderloin, or veal or pork tenderloin

steps: Beef, veal or pork tenderloin can be used; in this case pork tenderloin is used.
Cut the tenderloin across into suitable pieces and pound flat.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper and fry in a pan with brown butter over a brisk fire.
Arrange the beef on a very hot dish and pour over it the butter and gravy deglazed from the pan.
A few Maggi bouillon cubes can be dissolved in it.
Stir the butter and add the lemon juice.
With a teaspoon dipped in warm water, form small balls; these are rolled in the chopped parsley, and one ball is placed on each piece of beef.
Garnish with potatoes cooked in Palmin.

title: Fransk Omelet (French Omelet)
description: Prepared with egg yolks, powdered sugar, and juice.

ingredients.name: juice and grated zest from half a lemon
ingredients.sourceText: juice and grated zest from half a lemon

steps: Stir 6 egg yolks for half an hour with 6 dessertspoons powdered sugar and the juice and grated zest of half a lemon
Beat the egg whites stiff and fold in gently
Butter a mold, pour in the batter and let stand five minutes at low heat to set
Then place it in a hot oven and bake one hour
Cannot be removed from the mold
Serve with white sugar
The eggs must be stirred and beaten well and long, otherwise it will be heavy
Serves 5 people

title: Fransk Suppe (French Soup)
description: A soup made with beef, onion, and carrots.
steps: Cut 1 pound beef finely and cook it slowly together with 1 onion and 3 carrots in 3 quarts water until the meat can easily be pressed apart, which requires nearly 3 hours
To prevent the soup from boiling away, it is necessary that it cooks evenly in a pot with a tight-fitting lid
Add a large bunch of herbs and root vegetables and take them out when they are done
Strain the soup, place it back on the fire, skim it, and when it boils, add meat balls made from 1/2 pound meat
The soup can be smoothed with egg and eaten with toasted bread; this portion is for 3 persons

description: A cake made with apple, macaroons, and raspberry.
steps: Butter a form and flour it

On the bottom place a layer of small macaroons dipped in melted butter, then a layer of apple porridge, then a layer of raspberry marmalade, then again macaroons, and so forth, until the form is almost full
Beat 6 egg yolks with {{source-6}} and then with the 6 previously beaten egg whites
Pour this mixture over the rest, dust with powdered sugar, and then bake the cake 1 hour in a moderately warm oven
When done, turn it onto a dish

title: Franskbrød (French Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with yeast, egg white or water, and milk.

ingredients.name: egg white or lukewarm water for brushing
ingredients.sourceText: egg white or lukewarm water for brushing

steps: Dissolve the pressed yeast in the lukewarm milk and stir into {{source-2}} along with a little salt.
Knead the dough well until it releases from the hands and shows eyes.
When it has risen, shape without further kneading into small loaves.
Brush with egg white or lukewarm water and bake light brown with good, even heat.
If poppy seeds are sprinkled over the loaves before baking, they become the so-called Berkesbrød.

description: A bread preparation made with rice, wheat flour, and yeast.
steps: Boil {{source-0}} in a linen cloth or bag, ensuring sufficient room for it to swell.

title: Frikadeller (Danish Meatballs)
description: Prepared with beef, onion, and fat or butter.

ingredients.name: sweet milk and cream for consistency
ingredients.sourceText: sweet milk and cream for consistency

steps: Chop the beef very finely.
Mix the beef with kidney fat, eggs, hardtacks soaked in sweet milk, finely chopped onion, ground pepper and salt.
Work the mixture together until it becomes well aerated.
Thin with sweet milk and cream to achieve proper consistency.
Fry the meatballs light brown in a pan with fat or butter, using a spoon dipped in cold water to shape them.
Turn them on the pan and fry over gentle heat.
Brown butter in the pan, thin with a little water and serve with the meatballs along with stewed vegetables or carrots.
May also be made from other kinds of meat, fish forcemeat, or cooked or fried meat; in the latter case, mix the meat with 1 pound of fat, smoked, finely chopped bacon instead of kidney fat.

description: A pastry dish made with dough, apples, and raisins.

ingredients.name: approximately 10 good large apples, peeled and sliced
ingredients.sourceText: approximately 10 good large apples, peeled and sliced

steps: Bake preferably in a two-quart mold with roughly the same circumference at top and bottom
First make good pie dough
Place a layer of this in the bottom but not on the sides
Spread a layer of chopped and peeled apples two inches thick
Then spread a layer of chopped raisins
Sprinkle sugar, cinnamon and small pieces of butter over this
Then lay another layer of dough, then fruit and so forth until the mold is full
The top layer must be dough
Bake evenly for a couple of hours
When done, turn the bottom upward and before serving, sprinkle fine sugar over it
It is equally good when reheated

title: Frugt-Sauce af friske Frugter (Fresh Fruit Sauce)
description: A sauce made with powdered sugar, fruit or apples or pears or apricots or peaches or plums, and tapioca.

ingredients.name: (1 pound) rinsed fruit (apples, pears, apricots, peaches, or various sorts of plums)
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 kilogram (1 pound) rinsed fruit (apples, pears, apricots, peaches, or various sorts of plums)

steps: Set 1/4 liter water over heat with 125 grams powdered sugar, and when it is melted, add 1/2 kilogram rinsed fruit and cook until it can easily be pressed through a sieve.
Set the sauce over heat again and smooth it with mixed tapioca starch.
The amount of water and sugar must be adjusted according to the fruit's sweetness.
Some of the fruit may be left whole in the sauce; they are then cooked with the rest and removed before the remainder is pressed through the sieve.
Apples and pears must be peeled before cooking, and the cores removed.
Apricots and peaches are halved, the stones removed, and the kernels placed in the sauce.

title: Fyldt Hvidkaalshoved (Stuffed White Cabbage Head)
description: Prepared with cabbage, beef, and kidney.

ingredients.name: One good, firm white cabbage head
ingredients.sourceText: One good, firm white cabbage head

steps: Take a good, firm white cabbage head and remove the outer loose leaves. Cut off a lid the size of a saucer and hollow out the head. Fill with forcemeat of ground beef mixed with finely chopped kidney. Replace the lid and bind with a clean linen cloth or wrap with the removed large leaves and tie around it. Boil the head in about two hours in water with a little salt and butter. Before serving, drain the water from it. Serve with melted butter or brown sauce. To brown the head: after filling and binding with cooking twine, place it with a piece of butter in a pot with a tight lid to cook in its own juice over gentle heat until golden brown and tender, checking frequently so it does not burn. Place the head on a dish and remove the twine. Stir the sauce in the pot with a teaspoon of flour and pour over the head. The hollowed-out cabbage can be browned separately.

title: Gaas eller And med hvid Sauce (Goose or Duck with White Sauce)
description: A sauce made with goose or duck, fat, and mustard.
steps: Half-boil the goose while it is whole, then remove it and let it cool slightly
Chop it up on a board with a sharp knife and a hammer, first removing the legs and wings
Split the back and breast, and chop each of these parts into suitable pieces
Boil the soup when the chopped meat is returned to it; when it is tender, place it in a warm dish with a lid while the sauce is strained and prepared
Skim the fat well, take 2 to 3 spoonfuls and place on the bottom of the cleaned pot
Take 2 tablespoons of flour without heaping for a goose, stir it out in the fat and then fill it with the soup
If sour or sweet sauce is desired, it must be prepared in a tinned copper pot or enameled dish
Add mustard and a little cayenne, apples cut in 4 pieces, white root vegetables, and if desired, sliced almonds
If making the sauce without sweet and sour, make it stronger with seasonings, and use only root vegetables and meat balls
For duck, cook for 1.5 to 2 hours; for a whole goose, 2 to 3 hours or slightly less if very young
The bird should not be covered completely as it is better to spit-roast it; salt as you would other meat

title: Gaase-Ragout (Goose Ragout)
description: Prepared with goose, coloring, and wine.
steps: Either boil or roast the goose whole, or cut it into smaller pieces.
After rinsing the pieces in cold water, place them over heat in just enough boiling salted water with color so that the sauce becomes more concentrated.
Brown a slice of butter and bake flour in it, then thin with the strained and skimmed cooking liquid.
Give the sauce color with culinary coloring and add wine and paprika to taste.
Bring the meat to a boil in the sauce, serve with the sauce poured over, and garnish with boiled apple halves and puff pastry strips.

title: Gaase-Suppe (Goose Soup)
description: A soup made with goose, carrots, and celery.
steps: After the goose is plucked, singed, cleaned, and freed from feather follicles, cut off the feet at the knee joint
Cut off the neck and wings, then cut up the goose and remove the innards
Rinse the goose thoroughly
Place in a pot with enough cold salted water to reach the level of the meat
Scald the feet well, cut off the claws, remove the outer skin, and add to the soup along with the neck, cleaned gizzard, and heart
Save the liver for liver pâté
Once the soup is well skimmed, add bunch of herbs, 4 carrots, 1 celery, 4 leeks, and 10 whole peppercorns
While the soup cooks, prepare flour dumplings (recipe No. 497)
Peel {{source-8}}, cut into 4 pieces, remove the core, cook in water with sugar until tender but whole
Cook 1/4 kg (1/2 lb) rinsed prunes in the same water as the apples

When the vegetables are tender, remove them, cut into pieces, and place in the tureen with the apples, prunes, and flour dumplings (which should be cooked separately in salted water to keep the soup clear)
When the meat is tender, strain most of the soup off, leaving only a little in the pot to keep the goose warm
Skim the fat from the soup carefully and add the water in which the apples and prunes were cooked
If necessary, strengthen the soup with Maggis Bouillon cubes
Season with vinegar and sugar to taste, if desired
Serve the boiled goose garnished with parsley along with the soup and gizzards

title: Gaasesteg (Roast Goose)
description: Prepared with goose, apples, and prunes.

ingredients.name: 1 whole uncarved goose, about 5 to 5½ kg
ingredients.sourceText: 1 whole uncarved goose, about 5 to 5½ kg

ingredients.name: Maggi bouillon cubes or meat extract
ingredients.sourceText: Maggi bouillon cubes or meat extract

steps: Clean the goose by carefully removing all feather follicles and singeing it over a gas or spirit flame.
Remove the head with neck, wings, feet, giblets, and heart for soup or ragout; reserve the liver for liver pâté.
Make a crosswise cut at the rump, large enough only to remove the innards.
Remove the giblets and place in cold salted water along with any fat picked from the intestines.
Wash the goose thoroughly in cold water, rub the inside with pepper and salt, and fill with the 5 to 6 apples cut into 4 pieces each, along with the 125 grams of scalded pitted prunes.
Sew the goose closed, rub the outside with salt, place in a roasting pan, and put in a hot oven for a few minutes before pouring a little boiling salted water over it.
To ensure crispy skin, baste the goose only at the beginning.
Roast for 2½ to 3 hours.
Half an hour before serving, strain the pan drippings through a sieve and return the goose to the oven with very little water in the pan.
For the sauce, brown butter, add flour and bake it, then thin with the strained pan drippings from which all fat has been carefully skimmed.
Season the sauce with color, salt, and Maggi bouillon cubes or meat extract, as the goose drippings are not very strong.
When serving, remove the thread and garnish the goose with parsley (and with Danish flags if Christmas goose).
Serve with roasted or boiled potatoes, red cabbage, asparagus, preserves, and the apples and prunes that were in the goose.

title: Gaaſeſteg (Roasted Goose)
description: Prepared with goose, apples, and eggs.
steps: The best filling for a goose is apples and good prunes, which gives it the most pleasant taste, but others prepare a dough of eggs, bread and milk and fill with that.
You can also simply rub it inside with salt and pepper and then place a couple of anchovies inside; these are consumed entirely during roasting, but they give the goose a fresh and piquant taste.
Set it in the oven with water over it, which soon becomes fat, with which the goose is often basted.
It requires two to three hours of roasting depending on the condition of the oven and the size of the goose.
For sauce, sharp red wine sauce can be used, but in general a brown sauce prepared in the usual manner is used.
The fat is well skimmed off before the sauce is made.

description: Prepared with calf's feet and water.
steps: Scald the calf's feet, clean them and wash them well and place them overnight in lukewarm water.

title: Gelé til Fjerkræ og Fisk (Aspic for Poultry and Fish)
description: Prepared with meat or fish, vinegar, and white pepper.

ingredients.name: good soup, either meat or fish
ingredients.sourceText: 1 L good soup, either meat or fish

ingredients.name: 12 leaves of isinglass, rinsed in cold water
ingredients.sourceText: 12 leaves of isinglass, rinsed in cold water

ingredients.name: 2 to 3 cleaned and crushed eggshells, beaten together with egg whites
ingredients.sourceText: 2 to 3 cleaned and crushed eggshells, beaten together with egg whites

steps: Add a little vinegar, whole white pepper, salt, and a couple of bay leaves to 1 L of good soup, either meat or fish
When it boils, add 12 leaves of isinglass that have first been rinsed in cold water, and 2 to 3 cleaned and crushed eggshells that have been beaten together with egg whites
Stir constantly with a whisk and bring the aspic to a boil again and let it stand for a few minutes on the heat so that it does not set but remains clear
Pour it either into an aspic bag or through a fairly tight cloth laid in a sieve, and whatever is used for this must be wrung out in boiling water before the aspic is poured into it
If the first of the aspic that runs through is not sufficiently clear, pour it back again, and this must sometimes be repeated a few times
Pour a thin layer of aspic into the bottom of the mold; when it is set, arrange figures over it made from tomatoes, cucumbers, lemon slices, or red and white carved beets, with parsley as garnish
Pour another thin layer of aspic over this, and only when this is again set, place the meat or fish in it
Pour some of the aspic over it, which during the entire preparation has been kept near enough to the heat so that it is not set but only kept lukewarm
Make the aspic the day before
At serving time, dip the mold in boiling water if it does not otherwise release
Any leftover aspic can be filled into small molds, which when turned out are placed around the larger mold, or can be chopped coarsely and laid in a ring around the dish

Set it in a cold place, and when the jelly is stiff and is to be served, turn it out on a dish and lay preserved fruits around it.

title: Gjer (Yeast)
description: Prepared with hops, powdered sugar, and wheat flour.
steps: Monday morning steep 1 pint hops in 2 gallons water for half an hour
Strain into a crock and let cool until lukewarm
Add 2 level teaspoons salt and 0.5 pint best powdered sugar
Stir 0.5 pint wheat flour into some of the liquid, pour in and stir all together well
Wednesday morning add {{source-5}}, stir well and let stand until Thursday
Then strain and put into crocks with the lid loose for a day or two
Should be made two weeks before it is used, as it improves with standing
Store in a cool place and shake the crock so the yeast does not settle

Dissolve 0.5 pound brown sugar and salt in it

title: Glaseret Bayonne-Skinke (Glazed Bayonne Ham)
description: Prepared with ham, saltpeter, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: A good, meaty, fresh ham of 5-6 kg (10-12 lb)
ingredients.sourceText: A good, meaty, fresh ham of 5-6 kg (10-12 lb)

ingredients.name: ½ liter (½ pint) good broth or soup
ingredients.sourceText: ½ liter (½ pint) good broth or soup

steps: Remove the rind from a good, meaty, fresh ham of 5-6 kg and cut off the shank.
Place the ham on a trough or in a basin and rub it with a mixture of 1 kg salt, 60 grams saltpeter and ½ kg powdered sugar.
Let it stand for a week, but rub it daily with the brine that collects gradually.
Before roasting, wash it well and place it on the roasting pan with a few cloves, peppercorns, 1 bay leaf, 2 small onions, 2 carrots, 1 peeled and cut lemon, and ½ liter good broth or soup.

A ham of this size requires 3½ hours roasting and must, after being placed in the hot oven, be basted for the first two hours with 1 bottle of red wine and then sprinkled well with a mixture of breadcrumbs and powdered sugar.
If it does not become sufficiently crispy, sprinkle with more sugar.
Strain the broth, skim it and thicken it with sago flour.
Serve the ham hot with various vegetables or with macaroni, chestnuts, or purees.

title: Graa Ærter (Gray Peas Soup)
description: A soup made with peas, bouillon or broth or ham or stock, and wheat flour.
steps: Clean the peas and soak overnight in cold water
Place peas over heat with enough cold water to stand a couple of inches above them
Cook 2 to 3 hours under a lid, skimming well but without stirring
When almost tender, place a cast-iron pan over heat with {{source-3}}
Brown the butter to a light brown color
Add {{source-4}} and let it brown dark brown with the butter
Meanwhile, the soup should be cooked, strained, and fat skimmed
Place the browned flour in a pot and thin with soup until it becomes a smooth sauce
Add crushed cloves, a couple of bay leaves, vinegar, and sugar to taste
Bring to a boil
Drain the cooked peas in a sieve
Place peas in the tureen and pour the sauce over them
If the soup was made with smoked ham, serve the ham at the same time after removing the rind

title: Green Plums, Reine Claude (Grønne Blommer)
description: Prepared with plums, powdered sugar, and brandy.

ingredients.name: fully developed but unripe green plums
ingredients.sourceText: fully developed but unripe green plums

ingredients.name: powdered sugar equal in weight to the plums
ingredients.sourceText: powdered sugar equal in weight to the plums

ingredients.name: half a measure of brandy per pound of original fruit weight
ingredients.sourceText: half a measure of brandy per pound of original fruit weight

steps: The plums must be fully developed but not ripe.
After wiping the plums, cast them into boiling water but remove them as soon as they float on top and place in a sieve to drain.
Cook a thick sugar syrup with powdered sugar equal in weight to the plums.
Place the plums in the syrup, then immediately remove the pot from heat and let the plums rest in the liquid until the next day.
The next day, remove the plums and reduce the syrup until it becomes even, then pour over the plums and let cool.
Repeat this process on the third day and again on the fourth day.
On the fourth day, place the plums in the jar for storage and cook the syrup until it is even and thick, then set aside to cool.
When cold, stir half a measure of brandy per pound of the fruit's original weight into the syrup, adding it by spoonfuls with constant stirring in the same direction.
Pour the syrup over the plums and store in the usual manner.

title: Græskar-Suppe (Squash Soup)
description: A soup made with squash, vegetables, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: Sliced cooked leeks, meat balls, or baked French bread cubes (optional)
ingredients.sourceText: Sliced cooked leeks, meat balls, or baked French bread cubes (optional)

steps: Peel the ripe squash, remove seeds, and cut into small pieces.
Cook together with a bunch of herbs and some yellow and white root vegetables in some of the soup.
When vegetables are tender, remove and cut into pieces; place in tureen.
Remove the bunch of herbs and press well.
Pass the cooked squash through a coarse sieve by pressing with the remaining soup.
Bring to a boil.
Bind with 5-6 beaten egg yolks.
Season with salt and ground white pepper and arrange immediately.
In addition to the vegetables, add sliced cooked leeks, meat balls, or baked French bread cubes to the soup if desired.
Alternatively, the soup may be thickened with butter and flour baked together and diluted with the strained soup, in which case the eggs may be omitted.

title: Grønkaal (Kale)
description: Prepared with kale, wheat flour, and meat or salt or broth.

ingredients.name: 5 Potter Kjød- eller Saltmadssuppe (5 pots of meat or salt meat broth)
ingredients.sourceText: 5 Potter Kjød- eller Saltmadssuppe (5 pots of meat or salt meat broth)

ingredients.name: Raaskrællede, kogte og ituskaarne Kartofler (raw peeled, cooked, and cut potatoes)
ingredients.sourceText: Raaskrællede, kogte og ituskaarne Kartofler (raw peeled, cooked, and cut potatoes)

steps: Sprinkle the kale with salt water and let it sit for a few hours so that any insects fall off.
Pick the good leaves from the stalk and rinse well in cold water.
If desired (especially in autumn when kale has a strong taste), blanch the leaves: bring to a boil with water, drain in a colander, and rinse with cold water until completely drained.
Finely chop the kale with 3 tablespoons of wheat flour.
Heat 5 pots of meat or salt meat broth.
When the broth boils, gradually thin the kale with a little of it until properly diluted.
Pour the kale into the boiling broth along with some peeled onions.
Cook for about 10 minutes.
Before serving, add raw peeled, cooked, and cut potatoes.
If desired, add meatballs as you would for meat soup.

title: Grønkaal-Suppe (Green Cabbage Soup)
description: A soup made with cabbage and salted pork belly or brisket.

ingredients.name: 1.5-2 kg (3-4 lb) salted pork belly or brisket
ingredients.sourceText: 1.5-2 kg (3-4 lb) salted pork belly or brisket

steps: The soup for green cabbage is generally cooked in salted, striped pork belly or brisket.
While this cooks, remove the cabbage from the stems; rinse it well, squeeze out the water, then chop it very finely.
When the pork is cooked, skim the fat from the soup, and in this fat bake flour, which is thinned with the soup as in the previous recipes.
Alternatively, chop a couple of spoonfuls of flour together with the cabbage, which is added to the soup and cooked for several minutes.
The pork is served either cold or hot with the cabbage.

title: Grønne Tomater (Green Tomatoes)
description: Prepared with tomatoes, powdered sugar, and vinegar.

ingredients.name: Vinegar and water in equal parts
ingredients.sourceText: Vinegar and water in equal parts

ingredients.name: Vanilla bean or cinnamon stick and whole cloves
ingredients.sourceText: Vanilla bean or cinnamon stick and whole cloves

steps: Select small, oblong green tomatoes
Cook them in a mixture of equal parts vinegar and water until the skin can be removed
Boil sugar and vinegar together to make a syrup
Cook the tomatoes in this syrup for about 3 to 4 minutes, then pour the fruit and liquid into a crock
The following day, pour everything into the pot and give it one more boil, then remove the tomatoes with a slotted spoon and place in the crock
Let the syrup boil until very thick and pour it boiling over the tomatoes
The syrup can be cooked either with a vanilla bean for 2 1/2 to 3 kg (5 to 6 S) tomatoes or with a few pieces of whole cinnamon and 1/2 dozen whole cloves, according to taste
Seal immediately

steps: Shell the peas and cook tender with a bunch of parsley in salted water.
Reserve some whole peas for serving; strain the rest through a coarse sieve.
Brown 100 grams butter and 50 grams flour together and dilute with {{source-1}}.

Season with salt and sugar.
Serve with toasted bread. Small whole ripe tomatoes may be added to the soup.

steps: The evening before cooking, remove damaged peas and soak overnight in cold water
Place peas in a pot with enough cold water to stand about 4 inches above them
Add peeled small onions but no salt
Cook uncovered over moderate heat until peas begin to shed their shells, skimming but being careful not to remove the onions
When peas are soft enough to mash, stir with a flat spoon until they become like porridge
Place {{source-3}} over heat with 5 pots water

Thin the peas with the broth until they reach the consistency of gruel, adding boiling water if needed
Bring to a good boil with constant stirring to prevent scorching
Serve as hot as possible with the meat
For strained yellow peas, press through a sieve and thin with broth until smooth, then cook in a pot with chopped celery, parsley roots, whole peeled onions, and peeled apple pieces
Cook over gentle heat with constant stirring until roots are tender
Serve as hot as possible with the meat and toasted bread cubes

Boil, skim, and strain the broth as usual
Thin the peas with the broth until they reach the consistency of gruel, adding boiling water if needed
Bring to a good boil with constant stirring to prevent scorching
Serve as hot as possible with the meat

Serve as hot as possible with the meat and toasted bread cubes

title: Gule Ærter (Yellow Peas)

steps: Soak the peas in lukewarm water and let them stand until the next day.
Cook them in 3 L (3 pots) water without salt.
Cook the pork separately together with a good bunch, 2 celeries and 5 leeks.

Cut the celeries and leeks into small pieces and add them to the peas, which must be served very hot.
The pork is eaten with the peas.

title: Gulerødder (Candied Carrots)
description: Prepared with carrots, powdered sugar, and juice.
steps: Scrape and rinse the carrots, weigh them and cut into thin slices.
Cut the slices into fine strips.
Cut the lemon zest very finely.
Cook the lemon zest under a lid together with the carrots in enough water to barely cover them for about 15 minutes.
Drain the carrots through a sieve.
Boil 1/2 kg sugar and 1/4 liter of herb water together with the juice of 3 lemons to a thin syrup.
Add the carrots and boil for 5-6 minutes.
Drain the carrots again through a sieve.
Boil the syrup until it is very smooth to avoid having to boil it multiple times.
Add the carrots directly into the boiling syrup and mix well.
Pour into glasses and tie them up as soon as the preserve is ready.

description: Prepared with beef, onions, and wheat flour.
steps: Chop the cooked beef finely with onions, ground pepper, and salt to taste.
For each pound of beef, brown half a quarter pound of butter with 2 grated onions.
Finely chop the beef of 2 anchovies.
Brown the mixture with a little salt, ground pepper, and 2 teaspoons of wheat flour until it leaves the spoon.
When it boils, add one gill of beef broth for each pound of meat, egg yolk, and the chopped beef.
The hachis should be the consistency of a thin porridge.
Cook for approximately a quarter hour.
Just before serving, add a little rum or cognac.
Serve garnished alternately with browned potatoes and hard-boiled eggs cut lengthwise.

title: Hare (Roasted Hare)
description: Prepared with hare and butter or margarine.

ingredients.name: 1 unflayed hare weighing 5.5 kg (for 6 to 8 persons)
ingredients.sourceText: 1 unflayed hare weighing 5.5 kg (for 6 to 8 persons)

steps: Skin the hare as described for venison.
Cut off the head and forelegs, and place the hare on its back, then cut off the ribs down to the fillet.
On the inside of the back, break the spine in several places to facilitate carving.
Loosen all the membranes of the back, legs and forelegs with a sharp knife and remove them all at once without any meat following or being damaged.
Lard the hare on the back, legs and forelegs with fine larding strips, cover with butter or margarine and roast in a well-heated oven for about 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Serve with browned potatoes and red currant jelly or apple compote.
Carve and reassemble before serving.

title: Hareſteg (Roasted Hare)
description: Prepared with hare, onion, and bay leaves.

ingredients.name: A lump of fresh butter or the same amount of roasting fat
ingredients.sourceText: A lump of fresh butter or the same amount of roasting fat

steps: Skin and clean a young hare, removing all the innards and cutting off the head and bones.

Remove the inner skin from the meat, lard the roast and place it in the roasting pan with half an onion, three cloves, two bay leaves, some peppercorns and a lump of fresh butter or the same amount of roasting fat.
Sprinkle with a little salt and roast slowly, with repeated basting, approximately three quarters of an hour or somewhat more.
Add cream to the meat gravy, let it come to a boil, strain it, and serve it with the roast.

title: Havre-Suppe (Oat Soup)
description: A soup made with grains, bread, and water.
steps: Place 2 quarts of water on heat
When it boils strongly, sprinkle 1/4 pound of coarse oat grains into it
When they are completely cooked, strain the soup through a fairly fine sieve so that no grains pass through, and set it back on heat
Add sugar to taste, a little whole cinnamon stick and lemon zest
When it has come to a boil, pour it into the terrine
Prepare with preserved juice and serve with baked bread

title: Havresuppe (Oat Soup)
description: A soup made with oat grits, fruit juice, and preserves.
steps: Wash the oat grits in cold water. This rinsing is especially important when the soup is to be used for the sick, as grits often contain considerable dirt.
Boil 4.5 pots of water, and when it boils, add the grits and cook over fairly strong heat without stirring until it becomes an even soup, which will take approximately 3 quarters of an hour.
Strain the soup: place a hair sieve over an earthenware dish, add some of the soup to the sieve, stir the thin part through with a spoon and rinse the remaining grits with a little boiling water.
Empty the grits from the sieve into a dish and repeat with a new portion until all the oat soup has been sieved, ensuring the soup becomes appropriately even during sieving and dilution.
Return the sieved soup to the fire and bring to a good boil.
When ready to serve, season with sugar, juice and preserves to taste and serve with baked wheat bread cut into small cubes.
For sick persons, prepare the oat soup with only sugar and possibly a few drops of lemon juice or wine, but not with fruit juice or preserves.

title: Hel, Stegt Kalvelever (Whole Roasted Veal Liver)
description: Prepared with veal liver, lard, and coloring.
steps: Choose a good pale veal liver with a skin that bursts easily when pressed with a finger.
Soak in water for half an hour to draw out the blood, and remove the skin and veins as much as possible.
Lard the liver with fresh lard, brown it in butter in a pot, and add milk with culinary coloring and salt.
Roast gently for 1.5 hours, basting constantly.
Make a roux with butter and flour, and thin with the strained pan drippings until the sauce has the right consistency.
Add a little cold butter just before serving and pour a spoonful of sauce over the liver before it is served.
Serve with boiled potatoes.

title: Hele Appelsiner (Whole Oranges)
description: Prepared with oranges, sugar, and water.
steps: Score the orange peel with a sharp knife in uniform broad strips, removing every other strip so the oranges have a striped appearance.
Pierce the oranges several times with a pointed sharp knife or with a larding needle and lay them in cold water for one day.
Remove from water and cook in fresh water under a lid until the peels are tender to pierce.

Remove the fruit and lay on a sieve, and only when it has drained does it go into the jar and is covered with the hot, well-skimmed syrup, which is made from ½ kg sugar and 3¾ dl water to 1/10 kg fruit.
Cover the jar and set aside until the next day.
Pour off the syrup, boil it, and pour it hot over the fruit, which is again covered well.
After 3 to 4 days, pour everything into the pot and the fruit is given a boil, after which it is removed and placed in the jar.
Skim the syrup and reduce it until it is smooth; then pour it hot over the oranges.
Seal the jar immediately.

title: Hele Ribs (Whole Red Currants)
description: Prepared with currants, powdered sugar, and water.

Pick them carefully from the stems and only then weigh them
Cook sugar and water to a very thick syrup in which the currants get one boil
Remove them before they begin to burst and fill into glasses
Reduce the juice and pour it hot over them
Seal immediately

title: Henkogt Green Corn (Preserved Corn)
description: Prepared with corn, fat, and salt.
steps: Remove the husks and cook the cob until no white juice flows out when the kernels are pricked
Remove the kernels and pack in stone jars as follows: at the bottom a layer of salt 1 inch high, then corn in a 2 inches high layer, and thus alternately until the jar is nearly full
The top layer of salt should be 1 inch high
Pour melted but not hot fat over the whole
Press a layer of thick white paper that fits in the jar on top, which is tied securely with paper or a bladder
Store in a cold place
Soak overnight before use
Should the top layer show mould, remove it
The rest will not be affected

title: Henkogte Blommer (Preserved Plums)
description: Prepared with plums, water, and sugar.
steps: Prick each plum with a needle so the skin does not burst
For each 3 quarts fruit prepare a sugar solution of 0.5 gill water and 0.5 pound sugar
When the water is well warmed and all sugar dissolved, add the plums
Bring slowly to a boil and cook very slowly for 5 minutes
Fill into jars as directed above

title: Henkogte Perer (Preserved Pears)
description: Prepared with pears, water, and sugar.
steps: While 1 pint water with 0.5 pound sugar for each quart of fruit is heating, peel pears and place in cold water so they do not discolour

When the solution has come to a strong boil, add pears carefully so they do not fall apart; they cook until they can be easily pierced with a fork, whereupon they together with the solution, while it is still boiling, are filled into jars which are immediately screwed shut
Coarse and hard pears must first be cooked more in water and then placed hot in the heated solution, in which they cook 10 minutes before being filled into jars
Apples are treated the same way

Remove excess juice with a cup or ladle, and fill the tomatoes boiled into glass jars
